There have been numerous studies of the use of tacrine in Alzheimer’s disease and a meta-analysis1 found tacrine to have a small beneficial effect on both cognition and global clinical impression, although it was considered that the clinical relevance of these findings was unclear and that there were no data from long-term controlled studies. Some have considered2-6 that a cautious trial of tacrine may be warranted in patients with mild to moderately severe Alzheimer’s disease (although alter- native drugs are now available) and various guidelines on its use have been issued.5,6 The metabolite velnacrine has also been tried but does not appear to be effective, and is also associated with hepatotoxicity.7 1.
